issues.description: Pinning setuptools<82 as a runtime dependency in core/setup.py over-propagates a CI-only workaround.
issues.detail: The build_pkg and setup_mmcv pins are scoped to CI shell scripts and justified by the mmcv/pkg_resources issue. Adding setuptools<82 to core/setup.py install_requires forces the cap on every downstream user, not just the CI build. The invariant being maintained (CI can install mmcv) does not require constraining end-user environments. Scope the pin to the ray extra or to dev/CI only.

issues.description: FIXME comments lack a termination condition tied to the upstream issue.
issues.detail: Both shell-script FIXMEs point at mmcv#3325 but no mechanism alerts the team when it closes. A literate comment here would state: the pin exists because setuptools>=82 removes pkg_resources, which mmcv 2.1.0's build still imports; remove when mmcv ships a release that builds against setuptools>=82. Consider a CI check or a dated review.

issues.description: mmdet bumped from 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 without justification in the diff.
issues.detail: The PR title and comments address mmengine/setuptools, but mmdet also moves a minor version. No invariant is stated for why 3.3.0 is required (vs. 3.2.0 still working). If 3.3.0 is needed for compatibility with the new mmengine 0.10.7, say so in a comment; otherwise this is unaudited drift bundled into a CI fix.

issues.description: Using --no-build-isolation for mmcv silently couples the build to the ambient setuptools.
issues.detail: Disabling build isolation means mmcv's wheel build now depends on whatever setuptools the surrounding environment provides. That is precisely why the setuptools<82 line immediately precedes it, but the coupling is implicit. A one-line comment stating 'mmcv must build against the env's setuptools<82 because its pyproject doesn't constrain it' would make the invariant readable.

review.summary: This is a narrow CI fix pinning setuptools<82 to keep mmcv 2.1.0's pkg_resources-dependent build working, plus a switch from the mmengine git pin to the PyPI wheel. The shell-script changes are reasonable and the FIXMEs are honest about being temporary. The main concern is altitude: the same pin leaks into core/setup.py install_requires, which propagates a CI-only constraint to every AutoGluon user. Secondary nits are an unexplained mmdet 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 bump and implicit coupling introduced by --no-build-isolation. Overall UNDER-AUDITED rather than wrong.
